text: sleep-not-permitted 是一款适用于 DSH 的工具与提示词插件，通过 Cordis bundle 将守卫接入工具调用和系统提示。它识别 shell 前台等待命令、阻塞等待工具调用、重复轮询，以及需要交互输入或确认的命令；命中时拒绝调用并说明可行的后台重试方式。系统提示也会提醒 Agent 使用后台作业，完成后根据通知读取结果。可按需配置受管工具、等待时长、检测规则和消息语言。适合希望避免长时间前台等待占住 DSH 会话的用户。无需额外 API Key 或外部账号。

sleep-not-permitted adds a DSH tool guard and prompt guidance. It rejects foreground waits, blocking wait tools, repeated polling, and interactive commands, then suggests a background retry. Configure rules, wait limits, tools, and message language. No API key or external account is needed.
怎么避免 Agent 用 sleep 把 DSH 会话卡在前台？
希望重复检查进度时能提示我改用后台任务。
Can DSH reject commands that wait for terminal input and suggest a better retry?
sleep-not-permitted 的功能「前台等待拦截」：检查 shell 命令和阻塞等待工具，命中等待规则时拒绝调用，并给出后台作业或结束本轮的重试提示。
sleep-not-permitted 的功能「轮询与交互命令门禁」：重复运行相同检查命令或执行需要输入确认的命令时，返回拒绝说明；可通过配置调整检测规则。
dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · Introduction：

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · sleep-not-permitted：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH) plugin that forbids
**foreground waiting**. When an agent tries to run a command whose purpose is waiting
(`sleep`, `wait`, `tail -f`, `watch`, `ping` without `-c`, infinite loops), or calls a blocking
wait tool (`wait_agent`, `job_output` with `wait: true`), the call is rejected — and the rejection
is a set of instructions: run it in the background (`run_in_background: true`), or end the turn and
let the completion notice wake you.

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · sleep-not-permitted：Nothing is silently rewritten: DSH logs and shows tool arguments before dispatch, so a guard can
only refuse, not impersonate a different call. The plugin refuses, explains, and gets out of the way.

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · Why a plugin, and not AGENTS.md or a preset：- **AGENTS.md is per-workspace.** You would have to write the rule into every workspace, and every
  new workspace silently misses it.
- **A preset is per-agent configuration.** Every composition needs its own copy, and the user has to
  pick it.
- **A host plugin is profile-level.** Install once and every workspace, session, and subagent is
  covered. It can carry configuration, be upgraded, disabled, and removed.
section: Why a plugin, and not AGENTS.md or a preset

text:
dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · Why it is needed：A DSH session moves one step at a time: however long a foreground tool call runs, the session stops
with it. `bash({ command: "sleep 60" })` looks harmless but freezes the conversation for a minute,
and a five-minute `wait_agent` freezes it for five. DSH has a safety net for slow *work* (a
foreground command that exceeds its timeout is promoted to a background job), but that still burns
the timeout first — and waiting is not work at all.

So the plugin does two things:

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · Why it is needed：1. **Prevention** — a rule in the system prompt, next to the existing background-jobs section, so
   the model picks the background form first;
2. **Enforcement** — a synchronous `ctx.tools.guard()` denial when the foreground form is used
   anyway, with the retry spelled out.

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · What gets blocked：- **Waiting commands** in `bash` / `pwsh` / `terminal_send`: `sleep`, `wait`, `tail -f`, `watch`,
  `ping` without `-c`, `yes`, infinite loops, log-follow modes — see the rule table below.
- **Blocking wait tools**: `wait_agent` and `job_output` with `wait: true`, when the requested wait
  exceeds the budget (default **30 seconds**).
- **Polling**: running the same check command more than `pollRepeatThreshold` times within
  `pollWindowMs` — the "wait a little, check, wait a little, check" substitute for sleeping. It is
  refused with the same instruction: wrap the waiting itself in a background job.
- **Commands that need human input or confirmation**: `sudo` without `-n`, `ssh` without
  `-o BatchMode=yes`, login/key-generation flows (`npm login`, `gh auth login`, `ssh-keygen`, …),
  interactive editors and pagers (`vim`, `less`, `top`, …), `docker run/exec -it`, `read -p`,
  `rm/cp/mv -i`. They are refused in the foreground *and* in the background: a background job has
  no stdin, so it would hang silently — never settling, never notifying.

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · What gets blocked：If what you are waiting for has no DSH job handle (a remote host, an external service), be it a
command or a poll: wrap the waiting itself in a background job — for example
`ssh host 'until [ -f done ]; do sleep 5; done'` with `run_in_background: true` (sleep is allowed
inside a background job) — then end the turn; that job's completion wakes the agent. This is the
correct replacement for both `sleep` and polling when there is nothing local to await.

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · Behavior：- A foreground wait is rejected with `Error: <reason>`; the reason contains the exact retry form.
- A call that already has `run_in_background: true` passes — that is the shape this plugin wants.
- Ordinary commands (`git status`, `npm test`, `curl`, `grep`, …) pass untouched.
- `ask_user_question` is not a wait — it is you being asked — and is never blocked.
- Non-blocking reads (`job_output` without `wait`, `list_agents`, `team_task_list`) pass.

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · Behavior：The default budget (**30 s**) exists so short coordination waits keep working out of the box (DSH's
own Agent Teams guidance has the Lead wait for teammates). Waits above the budget — the five-minute
`wait_agent(timeout_ms: 300000)` case — are rejected. Set `maxBlockingWaitMs: 0` for strict mode:
not a single second of foreground waiting.

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · After a background job finishes：A completion notice means the job **finished**, not that it succeeded. The notice carries the
status (`completed` / `failed` / `killed`) plus the label; read the output and exit code with
`job_output` before continuing, and diagnose a `failed`/`killed` job instead of retrying blindly.

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · After a background job finishes：Background jobs have **no timeout of their own**. A job that dies mid-flight or hangs while waiting
for something that never happens never settles — and so never notifies. Bound it yourself: wrap the
command in `timeout N`, keep a deadline in retry loops, or write a marker/report file at the end.
For cross-machine waits the same applies to the remote wait loop: give it a maximum wait and let it
exit with a failure marker on timeout, so the local job always settles and always notifies.

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · After a background job finishes：If the work needs a human decision in the middle, do not background it: confirm first
(`ask_user_question`, or the DSH approval channel), then start it with non-interactive flags.

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · Rules：| id | matches |
|---|---|
| `sleep` | `sleep N` in command position (`sudo sleep`, `timeout 30 sleep`, `do sleep`, `&& sleep`, …) |
| `sleep-nested-shell` | nested shell payloads such as `bash -c "sleep 10"` |
| `sleep-script` | `time.sleep(30)`, `python -c "...sleep(5)"` |
| `wait` | the shell builtin `wait` |
| `tail-follow` | `tail -f` / `tail -F` / `tail --follow` |
| `watch` | `watch <cmd>` (re-runs forever) |
| `ping-forever` | `ping` without `-c` |
| `yes` | bare `yes` (endless output) |
| `infinite-loop` | `while true` / `while :` / `until false` |
| `follow-logs` | `docker/podman logs -f`, `journalctl -f`, `kubectl logs -f` |

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · Rules：Plain text inside quotes does not count (`echo "sleep 30"`, `grep 'sleep 30' file` pass);
in multi-line scripts, command position is evaluated per line.

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · Configuration：Override the bundle patch row from the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, or edit the plugin's
`cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: sleep-not-permitted
  name: 'dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted'
  config:
    enabled: true                 # false = turn the whole guard off

Invalid configuration fails loud at mount time (unknown rule id, empty `tools`, invalid regex,
non-boolean switch, unknown `language`) — there is no "installed but silently inactive" state.

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · Message language：`language: auto` (the default) follows the user's system language: it checks `DSH_LOCALE`,
`LC_ALL` / `LC_MESSAGES` / `LANG`, then the macOS system language preference, then Node's `Intl`
default, and falls back to English. A Chinese system gets Chinese-only messages and a
Chinese-only prompt section (roughly half the prompt cost); `both` emits both languages; `zh` /
`en` pin one explicitly. Resolution happens once at mount.

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · Install / uninstall：From npm (recommended):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted
```

Desktop profile (managed by the Electron app): install by npm package name
`dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted` in the plugin manager, or from the Discover / market panel.

Prebuilt tarball (no npm, no clone):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add https://github.com/JJJACKsong/sleep-not-permitted/releases/download/v0.4.1/dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted-0.4.1.tgz
```

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · Install / uninstall：From a local directory (offline or while editing):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/JJJACKsong/sleep-not-permitted.git

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · desktop: plugin_manager install_bundle with the absolute path of the cloned directory：dsh plugin --profile <profile> add /path/to/sleep-not-permitted
```

Uninstall:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · Tests：```bash
node --test test/detect.test.mjs test/plugin.test.mjs
```

- `test/detect.test.mjs` — detector positives and negatives (command position, quotes, nested
  payloads, false-positive protection);
- `test/plugin.test.mjs` — a minimal ctx double checks deny/pass, defaults, strict mode, message
  language, and fail-loud configuration.

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · Compatibility：Tested against DSH `0.1.5-rc.2` and `0.2.1-rc.3`. It relies on two host seams —
`ctx.tools.guard()` and `ctx.systemPrompt.section()` — and fails loud at mount if they change.

dsh-plugin-sleep-not-permitted README · Boundaries：- **Does not guess "might be slow".** `npm install`, `cargo build` and other commands that make
  progress still run in the foreground; the tool timeout promotes them to a background job
  (default 120 s, capped at 600 s).
- **Does not block work.** Long synchronous tasks such as `workflow` or `deliver_gate` are not
  waits and are left alone.
- **Does not rewrite arguments.** A denied call costs one retry round trip; the system-prompt rule
  is there to keep that rare.
- **Does not inspect script files.** How long `bash script.sh` sleeps inside cannot be judged
  statically; the tool timeout is the backstop.
